picks.file: Amstelredamum, nobile Inferioris Germaniae oppidum... - btv1b53178866m (1 of 2).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: hand-colored bird’s-eye view of the medieval city on the IJ, Oude and Nieuwe Kerk visible; later printing of the 1572 plate

picks.what: The Portuguese and High German synagogues, painting (Städel Museum, Frankfurt)
picks.why: Golden Age canal scene with the synagogues and the Zuiderkerk tower; best P2 view

picks.file: Gezicht op Amsterdam met de Beurs van Zocher, RP-P-OB-27.555.jpg
picks.what: The Dam with the palace, the Nieuwe Kerk and the new exchange, lithograph
picks.why: general view of the Dam; printed title says ‘after the completion of the new exchange’ (1845)

picks.file: Amsterdam (Nederland) Een Photochrom ((door middel van steendruk (lithografie) ingekleurde, SFA008002688.jpg
picks.what: The Singel and the Munttoren, photochrom print
picks.why: color canal scene with barges and the Mint Tower; record dates it about 1900

picks.what: Aerial photograph of the canal ring (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: the ring canals running up to the IJ and Central Station, Round Lutheran Church dome; black frame trimmed

picks.what: The Nieuwe Kerk and the Royal Palace on the Dam, photograph
picks.why: sharp color view of the Dam’s landmarks; the skyline candidates are grey or show only modern high-rises

notes: #19: Rijksmuseum gives 1835–1904, but its title and description place it just after the exchange was finished (1845). P4 alternatives: Gaston Braun’s 1864 rooftop panoramas from the palace dome (#21, #22, #26); not added as a second P4 view, being only 36 years before the photochrom. #10 is a flat fortification plan; #11–#18 are skull prints and a Piranesi of Rome.
